Reviewed recent pilot results (latency and cost), discussed burst planning and autoscale thresholds, and agreed on a benchmark with a simulated 2x-4x transaction burst. Redwood SE to provide autoscaling policy templates and cost deltas; customer to provide traffic traces. Next meeting scheduled after benchmark run.
topics: Pilot results review: p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization
Autoscaling policy options: reactive vs predictive
Burst capacity planning and warm pools
KV cache / prefix caching impact on cost
transcript: [00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll run about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos (Nexa): Carlos here, Rina, Samir and Leah on my side.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya here. Ethan and Maya are on as well.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. Agenda  quick results recap, dig into autoscaling and burst, action items. Carlos, any updates since last week?

[00:30] Carlos: We ran the pilot overnight, saw p95 around 210ms for the 1k token profiles but spikes up to 420 when concurrent users hit 800. We're using the Readwood dedicated pool config you gave  small spelling in the logs called it the "read-wood" pod, ha.
[00:44] Rina: The cost is looking ok but we worry about 3x holiday bursts, latency tail is the concern.

[01:05] Priya: Ok first thought  that tail looks like cold cache + autoscaler lag. On dedicated we recommend a small warm pool and a short predictive warm-up when metrics cross threshold. We can map that to CPU/GPU util and queue length.
[01:30] Samir: The autoscaler is k8s HPA in front of the runtime, right? We were expecting more deterministic scaling. Sometimes the HPA metrics lag us by 30s-60s.

[01:45] Ethan: Right  our suggestion is two-layer: immediate hot-burst lane using pre-warmed instances and a second reactive scaler for sustained increases. The hot lane can be kept minimal and used only when request rate exceeds X rps.
[02:10] Carlos: Can you quantify X? Our baseline is ~200 rps, holiday could be 800-1200 for short windows.

[02:22] Priya: For your profile, with our performance numbers a warm pool of 4 GPUs covers ~600 rps for the 1k token workloads; add burst capacity of 8 GPUs for 2x-4x events. We'll validate with bench run.
[02:40] Rina: How long to spin a GPU up? If it takes 90s we still see tail latency unless warm pool exists.

[02:52] Priya: Cold boot of a new node is 60-120s depending on infra; that's why warm pool + predictive signals (traffic anomaly detection) are crucial. Also, model variants help  smaller quantized variant for burst traffic to reduce token time.
[03:15] Leah: Wait, model variant fallback  does Redwood support an automatic fallback to a quantized variant? We don't want any manual overrides during live traffic.

[03:25] Ethan: Yes, we have routing policies that can fall back to compatible model variants by policy. That's in the config  you can route by latency or cost. The config can be canary or automatic failover.
[03:40] Carlos: Any impact on output quality with quantized fallback? We need to be cautious for fraud scoring flows.

[03:52] Priya: Small regressions expected; we can run evals on your prompt set to quantify. For scoring flows we can route to a hybrid  run a fast quantized pass for first cut, then async full model for final score.
[04:10] Rina: Security stuff  last meeting we flagged SSO, audit logs, and KMS. Where are we?
[04:18] Jordan: We're compiling the enterprise checklist. For Dedicated we support SAML SSO, audit logs exported to your SIEM, and integration with customer KMS/HSM. We'll send docs.
[04:30] Samir: We need to see retention and who can access logs  compliance requires 1 year retention and RBAC for log access.
[04:42] Maya (CSM): Noted  we'll include retention options. Jordan will share the security pack after the call.
[05:00] Carlos: About the pilot numbers  I can share token-level traces for the 72h window, that may help tune batching and KV cache policies.
[05:10] Priya: Perfect. The more granular trace lets us run synthetic bench with your sequence-length distribution and simulate KV cache hit-rates. That drastically changes cost estimates.
[05:30] Jordan: Speaking of cost, Ethan can you walk through the cost delta for the burst scenarios we modeled previously?

[05:36] Ethan: Yes; quick caveat these are rough. Baseline dedicated pool (8 GPUs) cost X. If you add a warm pool of 4 GPUs for steady availability that's +Y%. For 2x burst we estimate additional ephemeral usage that increases unit cost by ~22% over baseline for the burst window; 4x could be ~50% depending on cache hit-rate and whether you use quantized variants.
[06:05] Rina: Those percentages matter. Can we get a spreadsheet with scenario columns?
[06:10] Jordan: We'll send a cost delta spreadsheet. We'll also annotate assumptions: sequence lengths, tokens per request, cache hit-rate.
[06:22] Carlos: A question on autoscaling policies  are you recommending reactive HPA or predictive? Predictive sounds better but more complex.

[06:30] Priya: For short sharp bursts predictive + warm pool works best. We use a simple predictor (EWMA on rps + anomaly detector) to trigger warm-up. For longer sustained increases reactive is fine. You can combine both.
[06:48] Samir: How does this integrate with our cloud autoscaler? We have strict budget controls and can't auto-provision unlimited GPUs.

[06:55] Ethan: That's why we do a capacity budget: max burst capacity, pre-approved spending band, and a graceful shed policy. In extreme overload we can route to hosted cheaper tier (if data policy allows) or degrade to quantized outputs.
[07:15] Rina: Any concern about stateful things like KV cache when we scale down? Will we lose warm KV caches and increase cold starts?

[07:26] Priya: Yes, cache eviction affects tails. We recommend sticky prefix caching and LRU with a small grace period so when nodes scale in they hand off cache entries, but some coldness is inevitable.

[07:45] Carlos: Ok let's talk test plan. We'll provide the 72h trace. Redwood will run a benchmark that simulates normal load plus a 5-minute 2x burst and a 1-minute 4x spike. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, cold boot times, and cost metrics.
[08:05] Priya: Sounds good. We'll instrument token-level cost and latency. Also test a variant where we enable quantized fallback mid-burst and see output diffs.
[08:20] Leah: On evals  can you run our fraud prompts across quantized vs full model and give a diff report?
[08:29] Ethan: Yes, we'll run a small eval harness. Please provide the prompt set with expected outputs or metrics.
[08:40] Carlos: We'll anonymize outputs and share.
[08:45] Jordan: Action items noted. Any blockers from legal/procurement on Dedicated?
[08:52] Rina: Procurement is fine but legal asked about indemnity for model outputs and data residency. We need to see the Dedicated contract draft  can you share?
[09:02] Jordan: Yep, we can share a standard enterprise SOW and contract. I'll loop our commercial team and your procurement.
[09:10] Samir: One more technical  what's your expected warm pool memory footprint per GPU instance? We need to size NVMe and RAM for KV cache.

[09:20] Priya: For your model variant and 1k sequence length, expect ~45GB GPU memory per instance rim; NVMe KV cache suggested 200GB per instance to hold hot prefixes. We'll confirm after we run the synthetic bench.
[09:40] Carlos: That NVMe number seems high; can we get a lower config? We're trying to keep infra costs reasonable.
[09:46] Priya: You can trade NVMe for lower cache hit-rate and slightly higher latency/cost. We'll show tradeoff curves in the results doc.

[10:00] Jordan: Quick check  who's responsible for the benchmark infra? Redwood runs bench in our staging on dedicated pool but to mimic your network characteristics we can also run in your VPC if you prefer.
[10:12] Carlos: Prefer in our VPC to capture network egress and region nuances, but that requires security approval. We'll set up a temporary VPC peering and credentials.
[10:22] Maya: We'll provide a runbook for VPC setup. For quickest turnaround we can run an initial synthetic in Redwood staging and then a final in your VPC.
[10:35] Rina: Agreed. Schedule the staging run first so we can iterate quickly.
[10:40] Jordan: Ok. Timeline  Redwood to prep autoscaling policy by 11/6, Redwood to run staging bench 11/11, final in-VPC bench week of 11/17 pending creds. Does that work?
[10:54] Carlos: Yes, tentative works for us.
[11:00] Priya: I'll also attach policy templates: reactive HPA, warm-pool config, and routing rules for variant fallback.
[11:10] Samir: Good. A follow-up: when we do warm pools, do we pay for them continuously? We need to factor that into cost.

[11:18] Ethan: Yes, warm pool is reserved capacity so it's ongoing; that's the tradeoff  pay a small steady cost to avoid tail latency. We'll show cost per hour and amortized during expected holidays.
[11:35] Rina: On the routing policies, can we set per-tenant caps? We have internal product teams that use the same model differently.
[11:42] Priya: Yes, you can namespace routing and set per-tenant rate limits and quotas.
[11:50] Leah: Also can we enable tracing down to token level for debugging?
[11:57] Ethan: Yes, token-level tracing is available but it's heavy; we can enable it for bench windows and forward logs to your SIEM.

[12:10] Jordan: Let's move to risks and mitigations. Top risks: cold start tails, budget overruns, and model quality regressions on quantized variants. Mitigations are warm pools, burst budget cap, and eval-led gating.
[12:30] Carlos: Sounds right. Any red flags from Redwood side?
[12:34] Priya: Just to highlight storage of logs and keys  ensure KMS integration is scheduled early so we can validate encryption at rest for the Dedicated control plane.
[12:50] Jordan: Noted. We'll prioritize that before the in-VPC bench.
[13:05] Rina: Ok recap and owners?

[13:10] Jordan: Priya to send autoscaling template (AI); Ethan to send cost delta spreadsheet (AI); Carlos to send 72h trace (AI); Maya to send VPC runbook and security pack (AI). We'll reconvene after the staging bench.
[13:30] Carlos: One last thing  any competitors behaving differently on warm pools? Vertex had something called "preemptive scaling" that sounded similar.
[13:40] Priya: Many vendors have similar concepts; our differentiation is integrated routing and cost telemetry so you can see unit economics per-route.
[13:55] Rina: Great. Meeting end  thanks everyone.
[14:00] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and the sheet. Bye.
[14:05] Call ended
